To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
feature selection using weights from linear classifiers, such as SVMs, improves the classification accuracy of the three learning algorithms that we have investigated.
the feature selection based on linear SVM weights is a good choice for the large data sets and that the linear SVMs perform well when compared to the Naive Bayes and Perceptron classifiers.

• The linear SVMs and Perceptrons trained on a subset (a fraction) of the complete data set yield weights that are better suited for feature selection than the other feature selection methods investigated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1.
the development and analysis of feature selection methods that are suitable for large data sets and can be combined with a variety of machine learning algorithms.
the problem of feature selection in large document collections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
feature selection using weights from linear SVMs is a good choice for the classification of large data sets.
feature weighting methods based on the SVM classifier weights outperform the other methods.
the SVM based weighting method yields the best performance in the majority of cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is not only the compatibility of the feature selection method with the learning algorithm, but the sophistication of the method that is important.
we have shown that the weights from linear classifiers themselves can serve as effective feature selection criteria for document classification.

the feature selection method using linear SVM is a very efficient and effective method to select features for large scale document collections, and the feature selection method can be applied in combination with various classifiers, including the Naive Bayes classifier, the Perceptron, the Support Vector Machines, and the Maximum Entropy model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be very careful in selecting the feature selection and the classification methods for large data sets, as the two methods interact in a non-trivial way.

the sophistication of the weighting method rather than the compatibility with the learning algorithms improves the classification performance and that the weights from linear SVMs are a particularly effective feature selection method.
the sophistication of the scoring function is more important than its compatibility with a given learning algorithm.
